title: 计算机科学，从零搭建 · 第28部分：纠错码

chapters.Viterbi: 10. 卷积码与 Viterbi 算法
chapters.Outro: 回顾、习题，以及它们会在哪里再出现

eebf07e3104f.en: In 1947 Richard Hamming was running calculations on a relay computer at Bell Labs. During the week, operators restarted jobs that failed; at weekends nobody was there. <bookmark mark='a'/> The machine stored each digit in a two-out-of-five code, so it could detect a bad bit. When a check fired, it dropped the job and moved on to the next, and on Monday Hamming found his work gone. <bookmark mark='b'/> As he told the story later: if the machine can detect an error, why can't it locate the position of the error and correct it? <bookmark mark='c'/> His answer, published in 1950, started the theory of error-correcting codes. Two years earlier Claude Shannon had proved how far such codes could go. Closing the gap between the two took fifty years, and this part follows it.
eebf07e3104f.zh: 1947年，Richard Hamming 在贝尔实验室的一台继电器计算机上跑计算。工作日里，出错的作业有操作员重启；到了周末，没有人在。<bookmark mark='a'/>这台机器用五中取二码存储每一位数字，所以能检测出坏掉的一位。检查一旦报警，它就丢下这个作业去做下一个，到了星期一，Hamming 发现自己的工作没了。<bookmark mark='b'/>他后来这样讲这个故事：既然机器能检测出错误，为什么不能找到错误的位置并把它纠正？<bookmark mark='c'/>他在1950年发表的答案，开创了纠错码的理论。早两年，Claude Shannon 已经证明了这种码最远能走多远。填平两者之间的差距用了五十年，这一部分就沿着这条路走。

866c43aba94e.en: Here is a code you use every day. <bookmark mark='a'/> This QR code has twenty-five by twenty-five squares, and holds forty-four bytes: twenty-two of message and twenty-two of checks. You can scan it. <bookmark mark='b'/> Now paint over a piece of it, near the middle. Eight of the forty-four bytes are now wrong, and the decoder is not told which. <bookmark mark='c'/> And still it reads: CS, Built, Part 28. <bookmark mark='d'/> By the end of this part we will have built every step: the finite field, the Reed-Solomon code, and the decoder that found the message.
866c43aba94e.zh: 这是一种你每天都在用的码。<bookmark mark='a'/>这个二维码有二十五乘二十五个方块，装着四十四个字节：二十二个是消息，二十二个是校验。你可以扫一扫。<bookmark mark='b'/>现在把它中间涂掉一块。四十四个字节里有八个错了，而且解码器并不知道是哪八个。<bookmark mark='c'/>它照样读出来：CS, Built, Part 28。<bookmark mark='d'/>到这一部分结束时，我们会亲手搭好每一步：有限域、Reed-Solomon 码，以及找回这条消息的解码器。

7cc5a804ac58.en: Part 28 of Computer Science, Built: Error-Correcting Codes. <bookmark mark='a'/> In this part: the noisy channel and the simplest codes; Hamming distance and Hamming's code; the limits on how good any code can be, and a perfect code; finite fields, Reed-Solomon codes, and our QR code; cyclic redundancy checks, built from Part 5's shift registers; Shannon's theorem and the codes that finally reach it; codes for storage; and the frontier.
7cc5a804ac58.zh: 计算机科学，从零搭建，第28部分：纠错码。<bookmark mark='a'/>这一部分包括：有噪信道和最简单的码；汉明距离和汉明码；任何码能好到什么程度的极限，以及一个完美码；有限域、Reed-Solomon 码和我们自己的二维码；用第5部分的移位寄存器搭成的循环冗余校验；Shannon 定理，以及终于达到它的那些码；存储用的码；还有前沿。

3e2337df689e.en: Shannon's simplest model of noise is the binary symmetric channel. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each bit goes through unchanged with probability one minus p and flips with probability p, independently of every other bit. <bookmark mark='b'/> It is crude, but memory cells hit by cosmic rays, scratched disks and faint radio all behave like it to a first approximation. <bookmark mark='c'/> There are other channels: in an erasure channel a bit is lost but you know which one, and real noise often comes in bursts. <bookmark mark='d'/> Against all of them the tool is the same: add redundancy, so that the receiver can undo the damage.
3e2337df689e.zh: Shannon 最简单的噪声模型是二元对称信道。<bookmark mark='a'/>每一位以一减 p 的概率原样通过，以 p 的概率翻转，与其他每一位都相互独立。<bookmark mark='b'/>它很粗糙，但被宇宙射线击中的存储单元、划花的光盘和微弱的无线电，大体上都像这样。<bookmark mark='c'/>还有别的信道：在擦除信道里，一位丢了，但你知道是哪一位；真实的噪声也常常成串出现。<bookmark mark='d'/>对付它们，工具都一样：加入冗余，让接收方能把损伤撤销。

9856b80fed0c.en: The obvious code: say everything several times. <bookmark mark='a'/> Send each bit n times and let the receiver take a majority vote. It is wrong only if more than half the copies flip. <bookmark mark='b'/> With a channel that flips one bit in ten, three copies bring the error down to under three percent, nine copies to under one in a thousand. But the rate, the fraction of the channel carrying real data, falls as one over n. <bookmark mark='c'/> Twenty-five copies bring the error to about one in six million, and then only four percent of the channel carries data. <bookmark mark='d'/> Engineers in the 1940s assumed this was a law: more reliability always costs more rate, without limit. Shannon proved it false, as chapter nine will show. First, though, a picture.
9856b80fed0c.zh: 最显然的码：每句话说好几遍。<bookmark mark='a'/>每一位发送 n 次，让接收方做多数表决。只有超过一半的副本翻转，它才会出错。<bookmark mark='b'/>在每十位翻转一位的信道上，三份副本把错误降到百分之三以下，九份降到千分之一以下。但码率，也就是信道中承载真实数据的比例，按 n 分之一下降。<bookmark mark='c'/>二十五份副本把错误降到大约六百万分之一，这时只有百分之四的信道在承载数据。<bookmark mark='d'/>1940年代的工程师以为这是一条定律：可靠性越高，代价就是码率越低，没有尽头。Shannon 证明了它是错的，第9章会讲。不过先来看一幅图。

bbb4307c3dd7.en: Here is what noise does to a picture, and what codes do about it. <bookmark mark='a'/> A black-and-white image of three thousand eight hundred and forty pixels. <bookmark mark='b'/> Sent as it is through a channel that flips one bit in twenty, it arrives speckled: a hundred and seventy-nine pixels wrong. <bookmark mark='c'/> Sending every pixel three times and voting cuts that to twenty-two, but triples the traffic. <bookmark mark='d'/> Hamming's code, chapter three, gets sixty, while sending less than twice as many bits. Which trade is better depends on the channel; the rest of this part is about doing better than both.
bbb4307c3dd7.zh: 这是噪声对一幅图做的事，以及码能怎样应对。<bookmark mark='a'/>一幅三千八百四十个像素的黑白图像。<bookmark mark='b'/>原样通过一个每二十位翻转一位的信道，它满是斑点地到达：一百七十九个像素错了。<bookmark mark='c'/>每个像素发三遍再表决，错误降到二十二个，但流量变成三倍。<bookmark mark='d'/>汉明码，也就是第3章的码，错六十个，而发送的位数还不到两倍。哪种交换更划算取决于信道；这一部分的其余内容，就是要比两者都做得更好。

c1408844da8e.en: Hamming's first idea was a way to measure how different two words are. <bookmark mark='a'/> The Hamming distance counts the positions where they differ: these two words differ in two places. <bookmark mark='b'/> It behaves like a distance: going from x to z never costs more than going through y. <bookmark mark='c'/> On the binary symmetric channel, every flip makes a received word less likely, so the codeword most likely to have been sent is the one closest to what arrived. <bookmark mark='d'/> Decoding becomes geometry: find the nearest codeword.
c1408844da8e.zh: Hamming 的第一个想法，是一种衡量两个字有多不同的办法。<bookmark mark='a'/>汉明距离数出它们不同的位置：这两个字在两处不同。<bookmark mark='b'/>它像一个真正的距离：从 x 到 z 的代价，绝不会超过经过 y 的代价。<bookmark mark='c'/>在二元对称信道上，每多一次翻转，收到的字就更不可能出现，所以最可能被发送的码字，就是离收到的字最近的那个。<bookmark mark='d'/>解码变成了几何：找最近的码字。

0507187d7bfd.en: Picture all words of three bits as the corners of a cube. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each bit is an axis, and each edge is a single flip. The repetition code uses just two corners, zero zero zero and one one one, three edges apart. <bookmark mark='b'/> Around each codeword draw a ball: the words one flip away. The two balls do not touch, so any single flip is corrected by moving back to the nearer codeword. <bookmark mark='c'/> In four dimensions, take the eight words with an even number of ones, every other corner of the hypercube. Any two are at least two apart. <bookmark mark='d'/> A single flip lands on an odd word, so it is detected, but that word is equally close to several codewords: the error cannot be corrected.
0507187d7bfd.zh: 把所有三位的字想象成一个立方体的顶点。<bookmark mark='a'/>每一位是一个坐标轴，每条棱是一次翻转。重复码只用两个顶点，零零零和一一一，相隔三条棱。<bookmark mark='b'/>在每个码字周围画一个球：一次翻转能到达的字。两个球互不接触，所以任何一次翻转，都能退回到较近的码字来纠正。<bookmark mark='c'/>在四维里，取含偶数个一的八个字，也就是超立方体每隔一个的顶点。任意两个至少相距二。<bookmark mark='d'/>一次翻转落到一个奇数的字上，所以能被检测出来；但那个字离好几个码字一样近：这个错误无法纠正。

4d3cd615a792.en: The smallest distance between two codewords decides what a code can do. <bookmark mark='a'/> With distance d, up to d minus one flips can never turn one codeword into another, so they are always detected. And up to half of d minus one can be corrected, because the balls of that radius around codewords do not overlap. <bookmark mark='b'/> You can also trade: correct a few errors and still detect more. <bookmark mark='c'/> Erasures are cheaper than errors. If you know which positions are missing, any d minus one of them can be filled in, because only one codeword agrees with what is left. Chapter seven's QR code will use exactly this.
4d3cd615a792.zh: 两个码字之间的最小距离，决定了一个码能做什么。<bookmark mark='a'/>距离为 d 时，至多 d 减一次翻转永远不能把一个码字变成另一个，所以总能被检测出来。而至多 d 减一的一半次翻转能被纠正，因为这个半径的球互不重叠。<bookmark mark='b'/>也可以折中：纠正少数错误，同时检测更多。<bookmark mark='c'/>擦除比错误便宜。如果你知道哪些位置缺了，其中任意 d 减一个都能补上，因为只有一个码字与剩下的部分吻合。第7章的二维码正要用到这一点。

1a803e5fbf60.en: Hamming's construction fits in a picture. <bookmark mark='a'/> Draw three overlapping circles. Put the four data bits, here one zero one one, in the four overlapping regions, and choose a check bit for each circle's private region so that every circle contains an even number of ones. <bookmark mark='b'/> Seven bits are sent for four of data. <bookmark mark='c'/> Now the channel flips one of them. <bookmark mark='d'/> The receiver recounts: circles A and C are odd, B is still even. The flipped bit must lie inside A and C and outside B, and only one region does: it is d two. <bookmark mark='e'/> Every one of the seven positions sits in a different combination of circles, so any single flip is located and corrected, and with no flips, every circle is even.
1a803e5fbf60.zh: Hamming 的构造可以装进一幅图。<bookmark mark='a'/>画三个互相重叠的圆。把四个数据位，这里是一零一一，放在四块重叠区域里，再在每个圆独占的区域放一个校验位，使每个圆里一的个数都是偶数。<bookmark mark='b'/>为四位数据发送七位。<bookmark mark='c'/>现在信道翻转了其中一位。<bookmark mark='d'/>接收方重新数一遍：圆 A 和 C 是奇数，B 仍是偶数。翻转的那一位一定在 A 和 C 里面、B 外面，而只有一块区域是这样：它是 d 二。<bookmark mark='e'/>七个位置中的每一个都落在一种不同的圆的组合里，所以任何一次翻转都能被定位并纠正；没有翻转时，每个圆都是偶数。

e352bf185065.en: The same code as a matrix. <bookmark mark='a'/> Write the numbers one to seven in binary as the columns of a three-row matrix H. <bookmark mark='b'/> Codewords are the words that H sends to zero; each row of H is one of the three circles. <bookmark mark='c'/> If the channel flips position j, multiplying by H gives column j: the syndrome spells out the position of the error in binary. Our flipped word gives one zero one: five. <bookmark mark='d'/> The construction works for any number of checks r: two to the r minus one positions, all but r of them data. <bookmark mark='e'/> And the code is perfect: the balls of radius one around the sixteen codewords each hold eight words, and together they cover all a hundred and twenty-eight words of length seven exactly once. No space is wasted.
e352bf185065.zh: 同一个码，写成矩阵。<bookmark mark='a'/>把一到七的二进制写成一个三行矩阵 H 的各列。<bookmark mark='b'/>码字就是被 H 映到零的字；H 的每一行就是三个圆中的一个。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果信道翻转了第 j 位，乘以 H 就得到第 j 列：伴随式用二进制拼出了错误的位置。我们翻转过的字给出一零一：五。<bookmark mark='d'/>这个构造对任意个校验 r 都成立：二的 r 次方减一个位置，其中除 r 个之外全是数据。<bookmark mark='e'/>而且这个码是完美的：十六个码字周围半径为一的球各含八个字，合起来恰好把长度为七的全部一百二十八个字各覆盖一次。没有浪费任何空间。

fe5ba15e1219.en: Hamming's construction gives a whole family. <bookmark mark='a'/> With r checks the block has two to the r minus one bits, and the rate climbs towards one: a hundred and twenty bits of data for seven checks at r equals seven. But every block, however long, still corrects only a single error. <bookmark mark='b'/> So long Hamming codes suit channels where errors are rare and isolated, such as memory. <bookmark mark='c'/> The last row is the one in your server: sixty-four data bits, seven Hamming checks and one overall parity bit, seventy-two bits per memory word.
fe5ba15e1219.zh: Hamming 的构造给出一整个家族。<bookmark mark='a'/>用 r 个校验时，块长是二的 r 次方减一，码率逐渐逼近一：r 等于七时，七个校验带一百二十位数据。但每一块不论多长，都仍然只能纠正一个错误。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以长的汉明码适合错误罕见又孤立的信道，比如内存。<bookmark mark='c'/>最后一行就是你服务器里的那种：六十四个数据位、七个汉明校验位和一个总奇偶位，每个内存字七十二位。

fc6533b146f1.en: How much does it help? <bookmark mark='a'/> On a log scale: with no code, the error rate is just p. Three-fold repetition squares it, roughly, at a third of the rate. Hamming's code does almost as well at four sevenths of the rate. At one flip in a hundred, Hamming leaves under nine errors in ten thousand instead of a hundred. <bookmark mark='b'/> The simulated points agree with the exact curves. <bookmark mark='c'/> Hamming codes are still everywhere. Error-correcting memory stores each 64-bit word with eight check bits: a Hamming code plus one overall parity bit. <bookmark mark='d'/> It corrects any single flip and detects any two: part of the defence against cosmic rays, and against the Rowhammer attack of Part 5, though attackers have since found ways to flip several bits at once.
fc6533b146f1.zh: 它帮了多大忙？<bookmark mark='a'/>用对数刻度看：不编码时，错误率就是 p。三倍重复大致把它平方，代价是三分之一的码率。汉明码以七分之四的码率做得差不多一样好。在每一百位翻转一位时，汉明码留下的错误不到万分之九，而不是一百。<bookmark mark='b'/>模拟的点与精确曲线吻合。<bookmark mark='c'/>汉明码至今无处不在。纠错内存给每个64位的字配八个校验位：一个汉明码加一个总奇偶位。<bookmark mark='d'/>它能纠正任何一次翻转，检测任何两次：这是抵御宇宙射线、以及第5部分的 Rowhammer 攻击的一部分防线，不过攻击者后来找到了一次翻转好几位的办法。

39d52abcfc6d.en: Chapter four. How good can a code be?

73bfb0885b77.en: Every code trades rate for distance. <bookmark mark='a'/> For long codes, plot the rate against the relative distance, the minimum distance divided by the length: a code at delta corrects a fraction delta over two of errors. <bookmark mark='b'/> Some limits are easy. The Singleton bound: rate plus relative distance is at most one. Hamming's bound: the balls around codewords must fit in the space. And the linear-programming bound of McEliece, Rodemich, Rumsey and Welch, which is the best known for large distances. No code lies above the lowest of them. <bookmark mark='c'/> From below, Edgar Gilbert and Rom Varshamov showed that random codes reach one minus the entropy of delta. <bookmark mark='d'/> Between the two lies a gap, and it has been open for nearly seventy years. <bookmark mark='e'/> Nobody knows a family of long binary codes that beats random ones.
73bfb0885b77.zh: 每个码都在用码率换距离。<bookmark mark='a'/>对长码，把码率对相对距离作图，也就是最小距离除以码长：相对距离为 delta 的码能纠正 delta 一半比例的错误。<bookmark mark='b'/>有些极限很容易。Singleton 界：码率加相对距离至多为一。汉明界：码字周围的球必须装得下。还有 McEliece、Rodemich、Rumsey 和 Welch 的线性规划界，在距离大时是已知最好的。没有任何码能高过其中最低的那条。<bookmark mark='c'/>从下面看，Edgar Gilbert 和 Rom Varshamov 证明了随机码能达到一减 delta 的熵。<bookmark mark='d'/>两者之间有一道缝隙，它已经悬而未决了将近七十年。<bookmark mark='e'/>没有人知道哪一族长的二元码能胜过随机码。

b66accbe1a75.en: A few codes meet Hamming's bound exactly. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 1949 Marcel Golay published a code of length twenty-three carrying twelve bits, generated by this polynomial. <bookmark mark='b'/> We listed all four thousand and ninety-six codewords. The lightest nonzero one has weight seven, so the code corrects any three errors. <bookmark mark='c'/> A ball of radius three holds two thousand and forty-eight words, and four thousand and ninety-six such balls fill all two to the twenty-three words exactly. The code is perfect. <bookmark mark='d'/> Aimo Tietäväinen proved in 1973 that repetition codes, Hamming codes and this one are the only perfect binary codes. <bookmark mark='e'/> Its extended version carried Voyager's colour images of Jupiter and Saturn. <bookmark mark='f'/> And it builds the Leech lattice, which Henry Cohn and coauthors proved in 2017, building on Maryna Viazovska's method, is the densest way to pack spheres in twenty-four dimensions.
b66accbe1a75.zh: 有几个码恰好达到汉明界。<bookmark mark='a'/>1949年，Marcel Golay 发表了一个长度二十三、携带十二位的码，由这个多项式生成。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们列出了全部四千零九十六个码字。最轻的非零码字重量为七，所以这个码能纠正任意三个错误。<bookmark mark='c'/>半径为三的球含两千零四十八个字，四千零九十六个这样的球恰好填满全部二的二十三次方个字。这个码是完美的。<bookmark mark='d'/>Aimo Tietäväinen 在1973年证明，重复码、汉明码和这个码，是仅有的完美二元码。<bookmark mark='e'/>它的扩展版本传回了旅行者号拍摄的木星和土星彩色照片。<bookmark mark='f'/>它还能搭出 Leech 格：Henry Cohn 等人在2017年基于 Maryna Viazovska 的方法证明，这是二十四维里堆积球最密的方式。

7fe2b8a73259.en: The codes of the next chapters compute with polynomials, so they need numbers that behave like the rationals but come in a finite supply. <bookmark mark='a'/> That is a field: you can add, subtract, multiply, and divide by anything except zero. <bookmark mark='b'/> The integers modulo a prime form one. In this multiplication table modulo seven, every row contains exactly one 1, so every nonzero number has an inverse. <bookmark mark='c'/> Modulo eight it fails: two times four is zero, and two has no inverse. <bookmark mark='d'/> In any field, a nonzero polynomial of degree d has at most d roots. That one fact carries the Reed-Solomon codes. <bookmark mark='e'/> Évariste Galois found that there is a finite field for every power of a prime, and for no other size.
7fe2b8a73259.zh: 接下来几章的码都用多项式计算，所以需要一种数：行为像有理数，但数量有限。<bookmark mark='a'/>这就是域：可以加、减、乘，并且可以除以除零之外的任何数。<bookmark mark='b'/>模一个素数的整数构成一个域。在这张模七的乘法表里，每一行恰好有一个1，所以每个非零数都有逆。<bookmark mark='c'/>模八就不行：二乘四等于零，二没有逆。<bookmark mark='d'/>在任何域里，d 次的非零多项式至多有 d 个根。Reed-Solomon 码就靠这一个事实撑起来。<bookmark mark='e'/>Évariste Galois 发现，每个素数的幂都有一个有限域，其他大小都没有。

0f0be92beda8.en: Computers want a field whose elements are bytes. Two hundred and fifty-six is two to the eighth, so one exists. <bookmark mark='a'/> Read a byte as a polynomial whose coefficients are its bits. <bookmark mark='b'/> Addition is exclusive or. To multiply, multiply the polynomials and take the remainder modulo a fixed polynomial of degree eight that cannot be factored; QR codes use this one. <bookmark mark='c'/> Now take alpha, the byte two, which stands for x, and keep multiplying by it: one, two, four, up to a hundred and twenty-eight, then the reduction kicks in and gives twenty-nine. <bookmark mark='d'/> All two hundred and fifty-five nonzero bytes appear exactly once before the sequence repeats. Alpha generates the whole field. <bookmark mark='e'/> So every nonzero byte is a power of alpha, and multiplication becomes adding exponents: two table lookups and an addition, the way slide rules multiplied with logarithms. <bookmark mark='f'/> And multiplying by alpha itself is a shift and a conditional exclusive or: exactly the linear-feedback shift register of Part 5.
0f0be92beda8.zh: 计算机想要一个元素是字节的域。两百五十六是二的八次方，所以这样的域存在。<bookmark mark='a'/>把一个字节读作一个多项式，它的各位就是系数。<bookmark mark='b'/>加法是异或。乘法：把多项式相乘，再对一个固定的、不能分解的八次多项式取余；二维码用的就是这一个。<bookmark mark='c'/>现在取 alpha，也就是字节二，它代表 x，不断乘它：一、二、四，一直到一百二十八，然后取余开始起作用，得到二十九。<bookmark mark='d'/>在序列重复之前，全部两百五十五个非零字节恰好各出现一次。alpha 生成了整个域。<bookmark mark='e'/>所以每个非零字节都是 alpha 的某次幂，乘法变成指数相加：两次查表加一次加法，就像计算尺用对数做乘法。<bookmark mark='f'/>而乘以 alpha 本身，是一次移位加一次有条件的异或：恰好就是第5部分的线性反馈移位寄存器。

c2d00f512a46.en: Why that polynomial? <bookmark mark='a'/> There are two hundred and fifty-six polynomials of degree eight over the bits. Thirty of them cannot be factored, and any of those thirty builds a field of two hundred and fifty-six elements; in fact they all build the same field, labelled differently. <bookmark mark='b'/> Sixteen are primitive as well: the powers of x run through every nonzero byte. QR codes use one of those. <bookmark mark='c'/> AES, in Part 29, uses an irreducible polynomial that is not primitive, so its tables are built from the powers of x plus one instead. <bookmark mark='d'/> We checked all of them by brute force; Gauss's counting formula predicts the thirty, and Euler's totient predicts the sixteen.
c2d00f512a46.zh: 为什么是那个多项式？<bookmark mark='a'/>系数是比特的八次多项式共有两百五十六个。其中三十个不能分解，这三十个中任何一个都能搭出一个两百五十六个元素的域；事实上它们搭出的都是同一个域，只是标号不同。<bookmark mark='b'/>其中十六个还是本原的：x 的各次幂走遍每个非零字节。二维码用的是其中一个。<bookmark mark='c'/>第29部分的 AES 用的是一个不可约但不是本原的多项式，所以它的表是用 x 加一的各次幂造的。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们用暴力全部检查了一遍；Gauss 的计数公式预言了三十，Euler 函数预言了十六。

93ec275a2fdc.en: In 1960 Irving Reed and Gustave Solomon turned the root-counting fact into a code. <bookmark mark='a'/> Read the message, here three numbers, as the coefficients of a polynomial. <bookmark mark='b'/> The codeword is the list of its values at nine points. <bookmark mark='c'/> Three numbers in, nine out. <bookmark mark='d'/> Two different quadratics can agree at no more than two points, since their difference has at most two roots. So any two codewords differ in at least seven of the nine places. <bookmark mark='e'/> In general the distance is n minus k plus one: exactly the Singleton bound of chapter four. No code of this length and rate can do better. <bookmark mark='f'/> The arithmetic is really modulo a prime, one thousand and nine, but every value here is smaller, so you can picture it as an ordinary parabola.
93ec275a2fdc.zh: 1960年，Irving Reed 和 Gustave Solomon 把数根的事实变成了一种码。<bookmark mark='a'/>把消息，这里是三个数，读作一个多项式的系数。<bookmark mark='b'/>码字就是它在九个点上的值。<bookmark mark='c'/>进去三个数，出来九个。<bookmark mark='d'/>两个不同的二次多项式至多在两个点上相等，因为它们的差至多有两个根。所以任意两个码字在九个位置中至少有七个不同。<bookmark mark='e'/>一般地，距离是 n 减 k 加一：恰好是第4章的 Singleton 界。同样长度和码率的码，没有能做得更好的。<bookmark mark='f'/>运算其实是模一个素数，一千零九，但这里每个值都比它小，所以你可以把它想象成一条普通的抛物线。

96357873bd6c.en: Now damage the codeword. <bookmark mark='a'/> Three of the nine values arrive wrong, and the receiver does not know which. <bookmark mark='b'/> Lloyd Welch and Elwyn Berlekamp's method introduces an unknown error-locator polynomial E, which is zero exactly at the bad points. Then y times E equals f times E at every point, good or bad, and with Q standing for f times E, that is a system of linear equations. <bookmark mark='c'/> Solving it and dividing Q by E gives back the message, five, three, two, and the roots of E are exactly the three corrupted positions. The red points snap back onto the curve. <bookmark mark='d'/> With nine values and three unknowns, up to three errors can be fixed: half the redundancy. <bookmark mark='e'/> Erasures are even easier: lose any six values, and the three that remain determine the parabola by Lagrange interpolation. <bookmark mark='f'/> Real decoders use the faster Berlekamp-Massey algorithm, with Chien's search and Forney's formula; our QR decoder does.
96357873bd6c.zh: 现在损坏这个码字。<bookmark mark='a'/>九个值里有三个到达时是错的，接收方不知道是哪三个。<bookmark mark='b'/>Lloyd Welch 和 Elwyn Berlekamp 的方法引入一个未知的错误定位多项式 E，它恰好在坏点上为零。于是在每个点上，不论好坏，y 乘 E 都等于 f 乘 E；记 Q 为 f 乘 E，这就是一个线性方程组。<bookmark mark='c'/>解出来再用 Q 除以 E，就得回消息五、三、二，而 E 的根恰好是三个被损坏的位置。红点弹回到曲线上。<bookmark mark='d'/>九个值、三个未知，至多三个错误能被修好：冗余的一半。<bookmark mark='e'/>擦除更容易：丢掉任意六个值，剩下的三个就用拉格朗日插值确定这条抛物线。<bookmark mark='f'/>实际的解码器用更快的 Berlekamp-Massey 算法，再加上 Chien 搜索和 Forney 公式；我们的二维码解码器就是这样做的。

8b812a296217.en: Erasures are easier still. <bookmark mark='a'/> Suppose six of the nine values are lost, and the receiver knows which six. <bookmark mark='b'/> Only one quadratic passes through the three that remain, and Lagrange's formula writes it down directly: <bookmark mark='c'/> a sum over the surviving points, each multiplied by a polynomial that is one at its own point and zero at the others. <bookmark mark='d'/> Computed modulo a thousand and nine, it gives back five, three, two: the message, and with it every lost value. <bookmark mark='e'/> So a Reed-Solomon code repairs as many erasures as it has check symbols, twice as many as unknown errors. Chapters seven and thirteen use exactly this.
8b812a296217.zh: 擦除还要更容易。<bookmark mark='a'/>假设九个值丢了六个，接收方知道是哪六个。<bookmark mark='b'/>只有一条二次曲线经过剩下的三个点，拉格朗日公式直接把它写出来：<bookmark mark='c'/>对幸存的点求和，每个点乘上一个在它自己那里为一、在其他点为零的多项式。<bookmark mark='d'/>模一千零九计算，得回五、三、二：消息，以及随之而来的每个丢失的值。<bookmark mark='e'/>所以 Reed-Solomon 码能修复的擦除数等于校验符号数，是未知错误的两倍。第7章和第13章正用到这一点。

7594b1dc6d6e.en: Reed-Solomon codes are everywhere. <bookmark mark='a'/> Compact discs use two interleaved ones, and survive scratches thousands of bits long. Deep-space missions since Voyager pair one with a convolutional code, chapter ten's. QR codes use them, as do RAID-6 arrays and the storage systems of chapter thirteen, and modems, digital television and solid-state drives. <bookmark mark='b'/> The reason is that their symbols are bytes: a burst of bad bits corrupts only a few symbols. <bookmark mark='c'/> And they use erasures well: a dead disk or an unreadable spot is known to be bad, and each such erasure costs only one check symbol instead of two.
7594b1dc6d6e.zh: Reed-Solomon 码无处不在。<bookmark mark='a'/>光盘用两个交织的 RS 码，能扛住几千位长的划痕。旅行者号以来的深空任务把它和一个卷积码，第10章的那种，配成一对。二维码用它，RAID-6 阵列和第13章的存储系统也用它，还有调制解调器、数字电视和固态硬盘。<bookmark mark='b'/>原因是它的符号是字节：一串坏位只会损坏少数几个符号。<bookmark mark='c'/>而且它善用擦除：坏掉的磁盘或读不出的斑点，位置是已知的，每个这样的擦除只花一个校验符号，而不是两个。

2518e3fbf16a.en: Masahiro Hara's team at Denso Wave designed the QR code in 1994 to track car parts. Ours is version two: twenty-five by twenty-five modules. <bookmark mark='a'/> Three finder squares let a camera find the code and its orientation. <bookmark mark='b'/> Timing stripes and an alignment square recover the grid even on a curved surface. <bookmark mark='c'/> Fifteen format bits record the error-correction level and the mask, stored twice and protected by a small code of their own. <bookmark mark='d'/> Everything else is data: forty-four bytes laid out in zigzags two columns wide, then XOR-ed with one of eight masks, chosen to avoid large blocks and patterns that look like finders. <bookmark mark='e'/> We chose level Q: twenty-two bytes of message and twenty-two Reed-Solomon check bytes, enough to repair any eleven wrong bytes, or twenty-two missing ones whose places are known. <bookmark mark='f'/> Our encoder produces exactly the same modules as a standard library for every mask, so your phone can read it.
2518e3fbf16a.zh: 1994年，电装公司原昌宏的团队为了追踪汽车零件，设计了二维码。我们的是版本二：二十五乘二十五个模块。<bookmark mark='a'/>三个定位方块让摄像头找到这个码和它的朝向。<bookmark mark='b'/>定时条纹和一个对齐方块，即使在弯曲的表面上也能恢复网格。<bookmark mark='c'/>十五个格式位记录纠错等级和掩码，存两份，并由一个小码保护。<bookmark mark='d'/>其余都是数据：四十四个字节按两列宽的之字形排布，再与八种掩码之一做异或，掩码的选择是为了避免大色块和像定位图案的花样。<bookmark mark='e'/>我们选了 Q 级：二十二字节的消息和二十二个 Reed-Solomon 校验字节，足以修复任意十一个错误字节，或者二十二个位置已知的缺失字节。<bookmark mark='f'/>我们的编码器对每种掩码都与一个标准库生成完全相同的模块，所以你的手机能读它。

ee4b97048d10.en: Here is where each of the forty-four bytes lives. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each one owns a patch of eight modules, two wide, snaking up and down the code from the bottom right. <bookmark mark='b'/> The first twenty-two hold the message: a mode marker, the length, the text and padding. <bookmark mark='c'/> The last twenty-two are the Reed-Solomon checks, in the generator form used in practice: the message polynomial is shifted up and divided by a polynomial with roots at the first twenty-two powers of alpha, and the remainder is appended. <bookmark mark='d'/> So the whole codeword vanishes at those twenty-two points. The decoder evaluates it there: the twenty-two syndromes are all zero when nothing is wrong, and otherwise they encode where and how the bytes were damaged.
ee4b97048d10.zh: 这是四十四个字节各自所在的地方。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个字节占一块八个模块、两列宽的区域，从右下角开始在码上来回蛇行。<bookmark mark='b'/>前二十二个装消息：一个模式标记、长度、文本和填充。<bookmark mark='c'/>后二十二个是 Reed-Solomon 校验，用的是实践中的生成多项式形式：消息多项式上移之后，除以一个以 alpha 的前二十二次幂为根的多项式，把余数附在后面。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以整个码字在这二十二个点上为零。解码器就在那里求值：没出错时二十二个伴随式全为零，否则它们编码了字节在哪里、怎样被损坏。

71bb671d10b8.en: Here is the decoder working on the small scratch, step by step. <bookmark mark='a'/> It evaluates the forty-four bytes it read, as a polynomial, at the twenty-two powers of alpha. A clean code gives all zeros; these are not. <bookmark mark='b'/> The Berlekamp-Massey algorithm turns the syndromes into an error-locator polynomial, here of degree eight: the decoder now believes eight bytes are wrong. <bookmark mark='c'/> Chien's search tries every position and finds the eight roots, <bookmark mark='d'/> which are exactly the eight bytes the paint changed. <bookmark mark='e'/> Forney's formula gives the error value at each, and exclusive-or removes it. All forty-four bytes are back.
71bb671d10b8.zh: 这是解码器处理那道小划痕的过程，一步一步。<bookmark mark='a'/>它把读到的四十四个字节当作多项式，在 alpha 的二十二个幂上求值。干净的码给出全零；这些不是。<bookmark mark='b'/>Berlekamp-Massey 算法把伴随式变成一个错误定位多项式，这里是八次：解码器现在认为有八个字节错了。<bookmark mark='c'/>Chien 搜索逐个位置尝试，找到八个根，<bookmark mark='d'/>恰好就是被涂料改变的那八个字节。<bookmark mark='e'/>Forney 公式给出每处的错误值，异或把它去掉。四十四个字节全部复原。

364ce5cee285.en: Now we damage it, three ways. <bookmark mark='a'/> A small scratch whitens fifty-six modules. Eight bytes come out wrong. That is within the eleven errors the code can find on its own, and the text comes back. <bookmark mark='b'/> A longer blot ruins fifteen bytes. As unknown errors that is too many: the decoder's locator polynomial has no consistent roots, and it gives up rather than guess. But a scanner can see where the damage is. Told which eighteen bytes the blot touched, the decoder treats them as erasures, and twenty-two erasures are allowed. The text comes back. <bookmark mark='c'/> Paint a whole stripe and twenty-four bytes are touched: more than the twenty-two check bytes can cover either way. Nothing helps, and the decoder correctly reports failure.
364ce5cee285.zh: 现在用三种方式损坏它。<bookmark mark='a'/>一道小划痕把五十六个模块涂白。八个字节出错。这在码能自己找到的十一个错误之内，文本回来了。<bookmark mark='b'/>一块更长的污迹毁了十五个字节。作为未知错误，这太多了：解码器的定位多项式没有自洽的根，它宁可放弃也不乱猜。但扫描器能看到损坏在哪里。告诉解码器这块污迹碰到了哪十八个字节，它就把它们当作擦除处理，而二十二个擦除是允许的。文本回来了。<bookmark mark='c'/>涂掉整整一条，二十四个字节被碰到：两种方式下都超过了二十二个校验字节能覆盖的范围。什么都救不了，解码器如实报告失败。

73313af73631.en: Chapter eight. Cyclic codes and CRCs.

d68aa16595d7.en: Most of the time a network only needs to notice damage, and ask again. <bookmark mark='a'/> The cyclic redundancy check treats bits as the coefficients of a polynomial whose coefficients are zero or one. <bookmark mark='b'/> Append a few zeros to the message and divide by a fixed generator polynomial, here x cubed plus x plus one. Long division over this field is just exclusive or, with no borrows. <bookmark mark='c'/> Send the message followed by the remainder. Now the whole word is divisible by the generator. <bookmark mark='d'/> The receiver divides again; a nonzero remainder means something changed. <bookmark mark='e'/> In hardware this is a shift register with exclusive-or taps where the generator has ones, the linear-feedback shift register of Part 5, consuming a bit per clock. <bookmark mark='f'/> The thirty-two-bit version guards every Ethernet frame, zip file and PNG image. Ours agrees with zlib's on every test string.
d68aa16595d7.zh: 大多数时候，网络只需要发现损坏，然后重新索取。<bookmark mark='a'/>循环冗余校验把比特看作一个多项式的系数，系数是零或一。<bookmark mark='b'/>在消息后面补几个零，除以一个固定的生成多项式，这里是 x 的三次方加 x 加一。在这个域上做长除法，就是异或，没有借位。<bookmark mark='c'/>把消息连同余数一起发出去。现在整个字能被生成多项式整除。<bookmark mark='d'/>接收方再除一次；余数不为零，就说明有东西变了。<bookmark mark='e'/>在硬件里，这是一个移位寄存器，在生成多项式为一的地方放上异或抽头，正是第5部分的线性反馈移位寄存器，每个时钟吃进一位。<bookmark mark='f'/>三十二位的版本守护着每个以太网帧、每个 zip 文件和每张 PNG 图片。我们的实现在每个测试串上都与 zlib 的一致。

95409d02e332.en: In hardware the division is a shift register. <bookmark mark='a'/> Three flip-flops hold the running remainder, and exclusive-or gates sit where the generator has a one. The bit leaving the top is fed back into those gates. <bookmark mark='b'/> Clock in the message one bit at a time. <bookmark mark='c'/> After the last bit the register holds the remainder, one zero zero, the same as the long division on paper. <bookmark mark='d'/> Real network chips unroll the same algebra to process dozens or hundreds of bits per clock.
95409d02e332.zh: 在硬件里，这个除法是一个移位寄存器。<bookmark mark='a'/>三个触发器保存当前的余数，异或门放在生成多项式为一的位置。从顶端移出的那一位被反馈回这些门。<bookmark mark='b'/>把消息一个时钟一位地送进去。<bookmark mark='c'/>最后一位之后，寄存器里就是余数，一零零，与纸上的长除法一样。<bookmark mark='d'/>真实的网络芯片把同样的代数展开，每个时钟处理几十甚至几百位。

5aaae5bdc44e.en: What does a CRC catch? <bookmark mark='a'/> The received word differs from the sent one by an error polynomial, and the damage goes unnoticed only if the generator divides it. <bookmark mark='b'/> A burst, a run of errors no longer than the number of check bits, is a power of x times a polynomial of smaller degree, and the generator can never divide that. Our eight-bit CRC caught every burst we tried of length up to eight, thirty thousand of each length. <bookmark mark='c'/> Bursts of length nine slip through about one time in a hundred and twenty-eight, and random garbage one time in two hundred and fifty-six, exactly as the algebra predicts. <bookmark mark='d'/> The thirty-two-bit CRC of Ethernet catches every burst up to thirty-two bits and misses random damage once in four billion. <bookmark mark='e'/> But it is not a cryptographic hash: anyone can change a message and fix up the CRC. Part 29 builds hashes that resist that.
5aaae5bdc44e.zh: CRC 能抓住什么？<bookmark mark='a'/>收到的字与发出的字之间差一个错误多项式，只有生成多项式整除它时，损坏才会被漏掉。<bookmark mark='b'/>突发错误，即一串长度不超过校验位数的错误，是 x 的某次幂乘以一个次数更低的多项式，生成多项式永远除不尽它。我们的八位 CRC 抓住了我们试过的每一个长度不超过八的突发，每种长度三万个。<bookmark mark='c'/>长度九的突发大约每一百二十八次漏掉一次，随机的乱码每两百五十六次漏掉一次，与代数的预言完全一致。<bookmark mark='d'/>以太网的三十二位 CRC 能抓住每一个不超过三十二位的突发，随机损坏每四十亿次才漏一次。<bookmark mark='e'/>但它不是密码学哈希：任何人都能改掉消息再把 CRC 修好。第29部分会造出能抵御这种事的哈希。

3f197f68aaab.en: In 1948, two years before Hamming's paper, Claude Shannon had already settled the big question. <bookmark mark='a'/> Every channel has a capacity. Below it, at any rate, there are codes whose error probability can be made as small as you like by making them long enough. <bookmark mark='b'/> Above it, no code works. <bookmark mark='c'/> So noise does not force the rate towards zero, as chapter one's repetition suggested: it costs a fixed fraction. For the binary symmetric channel the capacity is one minus the entropy of p. At one flip in ten, fifty-three percent of the channel can still carry data with arbitrarily few errors. <bookmark mark='d'/> The entropy is Part 21's measure of uncertainty: the channel spends that many bits per bit on the noise. <bookmark mark='e'/> Compare repetition, which needed to drop to four percent of the channel to reach one error in six million.
3f197f68aaab.zh: 1948年，比 Hamming 的论文早两年，Claude Shannon 已经解决了那个大问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个信道都有一个容量。在它之下，任何码率都有这样的码：只要足够长，错误概率可以要多小有多小。<bookmark mark='b'/>在它之上，没有码能行。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以噪声并不会像第1章的重复码暗示的那样，把码率逼向零：它只拿走一个固定的比例。对二元对称信道，容量是一减 p 的熵。每十位翻转一位时，信道的百分之五十三仍能以任意少的错误承载数据。<bookmark mark='d'/>熵是第21部分的不确定性度量：信道在每一位上要花这么多位去对付噪声。<bookmark mark='e'/>对比一下重复码，它要降到信道的百分之四，才能达到六百万分之一的错误。

e3ef8ad33737.en: We can watch the theorem start to work. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take random linear codes of rate one half, and decode them perfectly, with a table of the most likely error for every syndrome. <bookmark mark='b'/> On a channel with five percent flips, whose capacity is point seven one, the block error falls as the codes get longer: from eleven percent at length eight to five percent at twenty-eight. <bookmark mark='c'/> At fifteen percent flips the capacity is below one half, and the error rises instead. <bookmark mark='d'/> Right at capacity it hardly moves. These lengths are tiny, so the trend is gentle, but its direction is Shannon's theorem. <bookmark mark='e'/> And here is the catch that took fifty years: decoding a random code needs a table with two to the n minus k entries. Shannon proved good codes exist. Finding ones that can be decoded fast was the rest of the story.
e3ef8ad33737.zh: 我们可以看着这个定理开始起作用。<bookmark mark='a'/>取码率二分之一的随机线性码，用一张表完美地解码，表里记着每个伴随式最可能对应的错误。<bookmark mark='b'/>在翻转百分之五、容量零点七一的信道上，码越长，块错误越低：从长度八时的百分之十一，降到二十八时的百分之五。<bookmark mark='c'/>在翻转百分之十五时，容量低于二分之一，错误反而上升。<bookmark mark='d'/>正好在容量处，它几乎不动。这些码长很小，所以趋势很温和，但它的方向就是 Shannon 定理。<bookmark mark='e'/>而这里就是那个花了五十年的难点：解码一个随机码需要一张有二的 n 减 k 次方项的表。Shannon 证明了好码存在。找到能快速解码的码，是后来的全部故事。

ee9df3af65b6.en: Shannon's argument is a counting argument. <bookmark mark='a'/> Send n bits; about p n of them flip, so what arrives lies close to a sphere of radius p n around what was sent. <bookmark mark='b'/> That sphere holds about two to the n H of p words, the typical errors of AI, Built's first part. <bookmark mark='c'/> Now choose two to the n R codewords completely at random, and decode to the codeword whose sphere contains what arrived. <bookmark mark='d'/> The chance that some other codeword also lands in that sphere is about two to the minus n times C minus R. <bookmark mark='e'/> When the rate is below capacity, that vanishes, on average over random codes, so at least one code is that good. <bookmark mark='f'/> The converse uses Fano's inequality: no code can push more than the capacity through. <bookmark mark='g'/> The proof constructs nothing. The practical codes that reach capacity, in the next three chapters, took another forty-five years.
ee9df3af65b6.zh: Shannon 的论证是一个计数论证。<bookmark mark='a'/>发送 n 位；大约 p n 位会翻转，所以收到的字落在以发送字为中心、半径 p n 的球面附近。<bookmark mark='b'/>那个球面上大约有二的 n H(p) 次方个字，也就是人工智能，从零搭建第一部分里的典型错误。<bookmark mark='c'/>现在完全随机地选二的 n R 次方个码字，把收到的字解码为球面包含它的那个码字。<bookmark mark='d'/>另一个码字也落进这个球的概率大约是二的负 n 乘 C 减 R 次方。<bookmark mark='e'/>码率低于容量时，它就趋于零，这是对随机码取平均的结果，所以至少有一个码有这么好。<bookmark mark='f'/>逆定理用的是 Fano 不等式：没有码能推过超出容量的信息。<bookmark mark='g'/>这个证明什么也没构造。达到容量的实用码，也就是接下来三章的码，又花了四十五年。

78f48e239966.en: Chapter ten. Convolutional codes and the Viterbi algorithm.
78f48e239966.zh: 第10章。卷积码与 Viterbi 算法。

1244e7807d9c.en: Hamming and Reed-Solomon codes work on fixed blocks. Peter Elias's convolutional codes of 1955 work on streams. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each input bit is shifted into a small register, and two parity bits of the register come out: rate one half. This message, one zero one one zero zero, produces these pairs. <bookmark mark='b'/> The register has four states, and drawing them over time gives a trellis: every possible message is a path through it. <bookmark mark='c'/> Decoding means finding the path whose outputs are closest to what arrived. Andrew Viterbi saw in 1967 that at each step you need to keep only the best path into each state; any path through a state that loses there can never win later. <bookmark mark='d'/> It is dynamic programming, Part 19's idea: eight comparisons per bit, however long the message.
1244e7807d9c.zh: 汉明码和 Reed-Solomon 码处理固定的块。Peter Elias 1955年的卷积码处理的是流。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个输入位移进一个小寄存器，寄存器的两个奇偶位输出：码率二分之一。这条消息，一零一一零零，产生这些位对。<bookmark mark='b'/>寄存器有四个状态，把它们随时间画出来就是一张网格图：每条可能的消息都是穿过它的一条路径。<bookmark mark='c'/>解码就是找出输出最接近收到内容的那条路径。Andrew Viterbi 在1967年看出，每一步只需为每个状态保留进入它的最好路径；在某个状态上输掉的路径，以后永远赢不了。<bookmark mark='d'/>这就是动态规划，第19部分的思想：每一位八次比较，不论消息多长。

f335285eb3f0.en: We sent twenty thousand random bits through the code at each noise level. <bookmark mark='a'/> With two percent of the channel bits flipped, Viterbi's decoder leaves about six and a half errors per ten thousand data bits, instead of two hundred. At half a percent, none at all. <bookmark mark='b'/> Real systems use registers with sixty-four states, and soft decisions: the receiver passes on how confident it is in each bit, not just a zero or a one. <bookmark mark='c'/> David Forney showed in 1966 how to combine codes: an inner convolutional code, and an outer Reed-Solomon code to clean up the short bursts of errors a Viterbi decoder leaves behind. <bookmark mark='d'/> That pairing flew on Voyager, and convolutional codes ran GSM, early Wi-Fi and 4G's control channel.
f335285eb3f0.zh: 在每个噪声水平上，我们让两万个随机位通过这个码。<bookmark mark='a'/>信道翻转百分之二的位时，Viterbi 解码器每一万个数据位只留下大约六个半错误，而不是两百个。在百分之零点五时，一个也没有。<bookmark mark='b'/>真实系统用六十四个状态的寄存器，并用软判决：接收方传递的是它对每一位有多确信，而不只是一个零或一。<bookmark mark='c'/>David Forney 在1966年展示了怎样组合码：内层一个卷积码，外层一个 Reed-Solomon 码，用来清理 Viterbi 解码器留下的短串错误。<bookmark mark='d'/>这一组合飞上了旅行者号，而卷积码支撑过 GSM、早期的 Wi-Fi 和 4G 的控制信道。

90e2a9cd6fad.en: Chapter eleven. LDPC codes and belief propagation.
90e2a9cd6fad.zh: 第11章。LDPC 码与置信传播。

d28476ab7615.en: In his 1960 thesis Robert Gallager proposed codes defined by sparse parity checks: each bit takes part in only three checks, and each check involves only six bits. <bookmark mark='a'/> Draw the bits on one side and the checks on the other, joined where a bit is in a check, as Michael Tanner did in 1981. <bookmark mark='b'/> Decoding passes messages along these edges. Each bit tells its checks how likely it is to be a one, from the channel and from the other checks. <bookmark mark='c'/> Each check replies with what the bit must be, judging from the other bits it sees. <bookmark mark='d'/> Repeat until every check is satisfied. This is belief propagation, the message passing of AI, Built's seventh part, and on a sparse graph each round costs time proportional to the length.
d28476ab7615.zh: Robert Gallager 在1960年的博士论文里提出了由稀疏奇偶校验定义的码：每一位只参与三个校验，每个校验只涉及六位。<bookmark mark='a'/>把比特画在一边，校验画在另一边，某位参与某个校验就连一条线，就像 Michael Tanner 在1981年做的那样。<bookmark mark='b'/>解码沿着这些边传递消息。每一位根据信道和其他校验，告诉它的校验自己是一的可能性有多大。<bookmark mark='c'/>每个校验根据它看到的其他位，回复这一位应该是什么。<bookmark mark='d'/>反复进行，直到每个校验都满足。这就是置信传播，人工智能，从零搭建第七部分里的消息传递；在稀疏图上，每一轮的时间与码长成正比。

72a6b2bbca5b.en: Here is the decoder at work on one block of our code. <bookmark mark='a'/> At seven percent noise, three hundred and forty-two bits arrive flipped. Round by round, the beliefs sharpen and the errors melt away: none are left after fourteen rounds. <bookmark mark='b'/> At nine percent, four hundred and thirty-two bits are flipped, and the decoder gets stuck at around three hundred, no matter how long it runs. <bookmark mark='c'/> But it knows: some parity checks are still unsatisfied, so a failed block is reported, not silently passed on.
72a6b2bbca5b.zh: 这是解码器处理我们的码的一个块的过程。<bookmark mark='a'/>在百分之七的噪声下，三百四十二位到达时被翻转了。一轮又一轮，置信越来越明确，错误渐渐消融：十四轮之后一个不剩。<bookmark mark='b'/>在百分之九时，四百三十二位被翻转，解码器卡在三百个左右，不论运行多久。<bookmark mark='c'/>但它知道：有些奇偶校验仍不满足，所以失败的块会被报告出来，而不是悄悄放行。

c12aa5b3cdac.en: We built a rate-one-half code of length four thousand eight hundred, with no short cycles in its graph, and decoded a hundred noisy blocks at each noise level. <bookmark mark='a'/> Up to seven and a quarter percent flips, every block came back perfectly. Then, within a percent or two, almost none do: the waterfall. <bookmark mark='b'/> Tom Richardson and Rüdiger Urbanke's density evolution predicts where the cliff falls for very long codes of this kind: eight point four percent. Shannon's limit for this rate is eleven. <bookmark mark='c'/> On the erasure channel the prediction is a one-line recursion, and we compute it exactly: point four two nine four, against a capacity of one half. <bookmark mark='d'/> Giving different bits different numbers of checks closes most of the remaining gap. In 2001 Sae-Young Chung, Forney, Richardson and Urbanke designed such a code within four thousandths of a decibel of the Shannon limit.
c12aa5b3cdac.zh: 我们造了一个码率二分之一、长度四千八百、图中没有短环的码，在每个噪声水平上解码一百个带噪的块。<bookmark mark='a'/>翻转率到百分之七又四分之一为止，每个块都完美恢复。然后，在一两个百分点之内，几乎全部失败：这就是瀑布。<bookmark mark='b'/>Tom Richardson 和 Rüdiger Urbanke 的密度演化预言了这类码在很长时悬崖的位置：百分之八点四。这个码率下的 Shannon 极限是十一。<bookmark mark='c'/>在擦除信道上，这个预言是一行递推，我们精确算出：零点四二九四，而容量是二分之一。<bookmark mark='d'/>让不同的位参与不同数目的校验，能填平剩下的大部分差距。2001年，Sae-Young Chung、Forney、Richardson 和 Urbanke 设计出了离 Shannon 极限只有千分之四分贝的这种码。

7dcd365a1fd4.en: The history is strange. <bookmark mark='a'/> Gallager's codes needed more computation than the hardware of the 1960s could give, and they were forgotten for thirty years. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 1993 Claude Berrou, Alain Glavieux and Punya Thitimajshima presented turbo codes: two convolutional codes, one fed a shuffled copy of the data, decoded by trading beliefs back and forth. <bookmark mark='c'/> They claimed performance within a fraction of a decibel of Shannon's limit, and many listeners assumed a mistake. There was none, and the decoder turned out to be belief propagation. <bookmark mark='d'/> In 1996 David MacKay and Radford Neal rediscovered Gallager's codes and found them just as good. <bookmark mark='e'/> Today LDPC codes run Wi-Fi, satellite television, ten-gigabit Ethernet, 5G data channels and the flash in solid-state drives. <bookmark mark='f'/> Turbo codes carried 3G and 4G, and spacecraft data since 2000.
7dcd365a1fd4.zh: 这段历史很奇特。<bookmark mark='a'/>Gallager 的码需要的计算量超出了1960年代硬件的能力，于是被遗忘了三十年。<bookmark mark='b'/>1993年，Claude Berrou、Alain Glavieux 和 Punya Thitimajshima 提出了 Turbo 码：两个卷积码，其中一个吃进打乱过的数据副本，解码时来回交换置信。<bookmark mark='c'/>他们声称性能离 Shannon 极限只差零点几个分贝，许多听众以为是弄错了。并没有错，而那个解码器后来被证明就是置信传播。<bookmark mark='d'/>1996年，David MacKay 和 Radford Neal 重新发现了 Gallager 的码，发现它们同样出色。<bookmark mark='e'/>如今 LDPC 码支撑着 Wi-Fi、卫星电视、万兆以太网、5G 数据信道和固态硬盘里的闪存。<bookmark mark='f'/>Turbo 码承载过 3G 和 4G，以及2000年以来航天器的数据。

4e6eed0e5a99.en: Here is Arıkan's construction for eight bits. <bookmark mark='a'/> Three stages of the same step: exclusive-or the lower wire into the upper one, first across halves, then quarters, then neighbours. <bookmark mark='b'/> Decoding takes the inputs in order, each using the ones before it, so each input sees a channel of its own. <bookmark mark='c'/> Start from an erasure channel that loses half its bits, and those eight channels already differ wildly: the first is almost always erased, the last almost never. <bookmark mark='d'/> So put the data on the four best channels and freeze the other four to zero, known to both sides.
4e6eed0e5a99.zh: 这是 Arıkan 对八位的构造。<bookmark mark='a'/>同一个步骤做三级：把下面的线异或进上面的线，先跨两半，再跨四分之一，最后在相邻之间。<bookmark mark='b'/>解码按顺序处理各个输入，每个都用到前面的结果，所以每个输入看到一条属于自己的信道。<bookmark mark='c'/>从一个丢一半比特的擦除信道出发，这八条信道已经天差地别：第一条几乎总被擦除，最后一条几乎从不。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以把数据放在最好的四条信道上，其余四条冻结为零，收发双方都知道。

5d10cd9743e7.en: In 2009 Erdal Arıkan found a code that provably reaches capacity, with a decoder as cheap as sorting. <bookmark mark='a'/> Start with a channel that erases each bit half the time. <bookmark mark='b'/> Take two uses of it and send u one exclusive-or u two, and u two. Decode u one first: it needs both outputs, so it sees a worse channel, erased with probability two epsilon minus epsilon squared. Then decode u two, already knowing u one: it gets two chances, so it sees a better channel, epsilon squared. <bookmark mark='c'/> Do it again and again. With each doubling the channels spread apart: here are the erasure probabilities of all of them, up to sixty-four. <bookmark mark='d'/> At a thousand and twenty-four channels, a third are already nearly perfect and a third nearly useless, and the middle keeps shrinking. <bookmark mark='e'/> The total capacity never changes, so the fraction that becomes perfect tends to exactly the capacity. Send data on the good ones, and freeze the bad ones to zero.
5d10cd9743e7.zh: 2009年，Erdal Arıkan 找到了一种可证明达到容量的码，解码器和排序一样便宜。<bookmark mark='a'/>从一个一半时间擦除每一位的信道出发。<bookmark mark='b'/>用它两次，发送 u 一异或 u 二，以及 u 二。先解码 u 一：它需要两个输出，所以它看到一条更差的信道，擦除概率是二 epsilon 减 epsilon 平方。再在已知 u 一的情况下解码 u 二：它有两次机会，所以看到一条更好的信道，epsilon 平方。<bookmark mark='c'/>一遍又一遍地做。每翻一倍，信道就更加分化：这里是直到六十四条时全部信道的擦除概率。<bookmark mark='d'/>到一千零二十四条信道时，已有三分之一近乎完美，三分之一近乎无用，中间的还在不断缩小。<bookmark mark='e'/>总容量始终不变，所以变得完美的比例恰好趋于容量。把数据放在好的上面，把坏的冻结为零。

144d5b691176.en: Decoding follows the construction. <bookmark mark='a'/> Decode the bits one at a time, each using the decisions already made, in time N log N. <bookmark mark='b'/> We sent rate-one-half polar codes over the binary symmetric channel. Well below capacity, the longer code makes fewer mistakes; as the channel approaches capacity, both collapse. <bookmark mark='c'/> At practical lengths, plain successive cancellation is not the best decoder. Ido Tal and Alexander Vardy keep a short list of candidate paths and use a CRC, chapter eight's, to pick the right one. <bookmark mark='d'/> In 2016 the standards body for 5G chose polar codes for the control channels and LDPC codes for data: ten years from Arıkan's paper to billions of phones.
144d5b691176.zh: 解码沿着构造进行。<bookmark mark='a'/>一次解码一位，每位都用到已经做出的判决，时间是 N log N。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们在二元对称信道上发送码率二分之一的极化码。远低于容量时，较长的码出错更少；当信道逼近容量，两者都崩溃。<bookmark mark='c'/>在实际码长下，朴素的逐次消除并不是最好的解码器。Ido Tal 和 Alexander Vardy 保留一个候选路径的短列表，再用第8章的 CRC 挑出正确的那条。<bookmark mark='d'/>2016年，5G 的标准组织为控制信道选择了极化码，为数据选择了 LDPC 码：从 Arıkan 的论文到几十亿部手机，十年。

3582a0b9e398.en: Storage is the erasure channel: a dead disk is known to be dead. <bookmark mark='a'/> RAID-5 adds one disk holding the exclusive or of all the others, byte by byte, and so can rebuild any one that fails. <bookmark mark='b'/> RAID-6 adds a second check disk, a weighted sum in the field of chapter five, with a different power of g for each disk. <bookmark mark='c'/> If two disks die, each byte position gives two equations in two unknowns, and the field lets us solve them. <bookmark mark='d'/> We rebuilt both lost disks exactly. <bookmark mark='e'/> This is a Reed-Solomon code with two check symbols, read across the disks; Linux implements it this way, following Peter Anvin.
3582a0b9e398.zh: 存储就是擦除信道：坏掉的磁盘，大家都知道它坏了。<bookmark mark='a'/>RAID-5 加一块磁盘，逐字节存放其余所有磁盘的异或，所以任何一块坏掉都能重建。<bookmark mark='b'/>RAID-6 再加一块校验盘，是第5章那个域里的加权和，每块磁盘用 g 的不同次幂。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果两块磁盘坏掉，每个字节位置给出两个方程、两个未知数，而域让我们能解出它们。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们把两块丢失的磁盘精确地重建了。<bookmark mark='e'/>这是一个有两个校验符号的 Reed-Solomon 码，横跨各磁盘来读；Linux 按照 Peter Anvin 的方式这样实现它。

f1cee8172a59.en: At data-centre scale, machines fail every day. <bookmark mark='a'/> The simple defence is three copies of everything, which triples the disks. <bookmark mark='b'/> A Reed-Solomon code that splits each block into ten pieces and adds four checks survives any four losses using only one point four times the space. Facebook's f4 warm storage and Hadoop's file system use exactly this. <bookmark mark='c'/> The price is repair: rebuilding one lost piece means reading ten others over the network. <bookmark mark='d'/> Microsoft's Azure storage adds a little more parity, one per local group of six, so the common single repair reads only six pieces. <bookmark mark='e'/> How little you must read to repair, for a given amount of storage, became a research field of its own.
f1cee8172a59.zh: 在数据中心的规模上，机器每天都在坏。<bookmark mark='a'/>简单的防御是每样东西存三份，磁盘数变成三倍。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个把每块数据分成十份、再加四个校验的 Reed-Solomon 码，能扛住任意四份丢失，只用一点四倍的空间。Facebook 的 f4 温存储和 Hadoop 的文件系统用的正是这个。<bookmark mark='c'/>代价在修复：重建丢失的一份，要通过网络读取另外十份。<bookmark mark='d'/>微软的 Azure 存储多加一点校验，每个六份的本地组一个，所以常见的单份修复只需读六份。<bookmark mark='e'/>在给定存储量下，修复时最少要读多少，自成了一个研究领域。

9c8a1137ec4f.en: One more storage and broadcast trick. <bookmark mark='a'/> Michael Luby's LT codes, from 2002, make each output block the exclusive or of a random handful of source blocks. <bookmark mark='b'/> The sender can produce outputs forever, like a fountain, and a receiver just collects enough of them, from any source, in any order, whichever ones arrive. <bookmark mark='c'/> Decoding peels: any output with a single unknown source reveals it, which is substituted everywhere, and the process repeats. <bookmark mark='d'/> With Luby's robust soliton distribution of degrees, we needed about thirty percent extra blocks for a hundred source blocks, eighteen percent for a thousand, and nine percent for ten thousand. <bookmark mark='e'/> Amin Shokrollahi's Raptor codes add a precode and bring the overhead to a few percent; they carry broadcast video and multimedia in mobile networks.
9c8a1137ec4f.zh: 再来一个存储和广播的技巧。<bookmark mark='a'/>Michael Luby 2002年的 LT 码，让每个输出块是随机一小撮源块的异或。<bookmark mark='b'/>发送方可以像喷泉一样永远产生输出，接收方只要收集到足够多，从任何来源、按任何顺序，到了哪些算哪些。<bookmark mark='c'/>解码靠剥离：只含一个未知源块的输出就揭示了它，把它代入各处，如此反复。<bookmark mark='d'/>用 Luby 的鲁棒孤波度分布，一百个源块我们需要多出大约百分之三十的块，一千个要百分之十八，一万个要百分之九。<bookmark mark='e'/>Amin Shokrollahi 的 Raptor 码加了一个预编码，把开销降到百分之几；它们承载着移动网络中的广播视频和多媒体。

c1ea347974d6.en: Chapter fourteen. The frontier: capacity and locality.
c1ea347974d6.zh: 第14章。前沿：容量与局部性。

0049ecf64976.en: Some of the newest results are about the oldest codes. <bookmark mark='a'/> Reed-Muller codes, from 1954, evaluate low-degree polynomials in many variables. <bookmark mark='b'/> Do they reach Shannon's capacity? On erasure channels, Shrinivas Kudekar and coauthors proved yes in 2016, using only the codes' symmetry. <bookmark mark='c'/> For every binary symmetric channel, Emmanuel Abbe and Colin Sandon proved it in 2023, nearly seventy years after the codes were invented. <bookmark mark='d'/> Another idea: when there are too many errors to decode uniquely, return a short list of candidates. <bookmark mark='e'/> Madhu Sudan showed in 1997 that Reed-Solomon codes can be list-decoded well past half their distance. <bookmark mark='f'/> And Venkatesan Guruswami and Atri Rudra found folded Reed-Solomon codes that correct a fraction of errors approaching one minus the rate: the best possible.
0049ecf64976.zh: 一些最新的结果，关于的是最老的码。<bookmark mark='a'/>Reed-Muller 码始于1954年，它对多元低次多项式求值。<bookmark mark='b'/>它们能达到 Shannon 容量吗？在擦除信道上，Shrinivas Kudekar 等人在2016年证明了能，只用到这些码的对称性。<bookmark mark='c'/>对每个二元对称信道，Emmanuel Abbe 和 Colin Sandon 在2023年证明了它，距这些码诞生将近七十年。<bookmark mark='d'/>另一个想法：错误多到无法唯一解码时，返回一个短的候选列表。<bookmark mark='e'/>Madhu Sudan 在1997年证明，Reed-Solomon 码可以列表解码，远远超过距离的一半。<bookmark mark='f'/>而 Venkatesan Guruswami 和 Atri Rudra 找到了折叠 Reed-Solomon 码，能纠正的错误比例逼近一减码率：这是可能的最好结果。

354d548d3539.en: Sometimes you need one bit of a huge encoded file, not all of it. <bookmark mark='a'/> The Hadamard code stores every parity of the message. To learn bit i, read the codeword at a random position a and at a with bit i flipped; their exclusive or is the bit. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each of the two reads lands on a uniformly random position, so if a fraction delta is corrupted, the answer is right with probability at least one minus two delta. Our measurements sit just above that line, and a majority over fifteen pairs is nearly always right. <bookmark mark='c'/> This is a locally decodable code, the cousin of Part 27's linearity test. <bookmark mark='d'/> The price is length: two to the k positions for k bits. How short a code readable with two or three queries can be is a major open problem, with huge gaps between the bounds.
354d548d3539.zh: 有时你只需要一个巨大编码文件里的一位，而不是全部。<bookmark mark='a'/>Hadamard 码存储消息的每一种奇偶。要得到第 i 位，就在一个随机位置 a 和把 a 的第 i 位翻转后的位置各读一次码字；两者的异或就是这一位。<bookmark mark='b'/>两次读取各自落在一个均匀随机的位置上，所以如果有 delta 比例被损坏，答案正确的概率至少是一减二 delta。我们的测量值正好略高于这条线，而对十五对读取取多数几乎总是对的。<bookmark mark='c'/>这是一种局部可解码码，第27部分线性性测试的近亲。<bookmark mark='d'/>代价是长度：k 位要二的 k 次方个位置。只读两三次就能解码的码最短能有多短，是一个重大的未解问题，上下界之间差距巨大。

621e677cb2bf.en: Two linked breakthroughs came in 2021. <bookmark mark='a'/> A locally testable code lets you check, by reading a few random symbols, whether a word is a codeword or far from every codeword. <bookmark mark='b'/> For decades nobody knew whether such codes could also have constant rate and constant relative distance, the c-cubed codes. <bookmark mark='c'/> Irit Dinur, Shai Evra, Ron Livne, Alexander Lubotzky and Shahar Mozes built them, and so, independently, did Pavel Panteleev and Gleb Kalachev, using high-dimensional expanders. <bookmark mark='d'/> Panteleev and Kalachev's construction also gave the first good quantum LDPC codes, answering a twenty-year-old question. <bookmark mark='e'/> Quantum computers cannot work at all without error correction, as Part 53 shows. <bookmark mark='f'/> And locally testable codes are what the PCP theorems of Part 27 are made of.
621e677cb2bf.zh: 2021年出现了两项相互关联的突破。<bookmark mark='a'/>局部可测试码让你只读几个随机符号，就能判断一个字是码字，还是离每个码字都很远。<bookmark mark='b'/>几十年来，没人知道这样的码能否同时具有常数码率和常数相对距离，也就是所谓的 c 立方码。<bookmark mark='c'/>Irit Dinur、Shai Evra、Ron Livne、Alexander Lubotzky 和 Shahar Mozes 造出了它们，Pavel Panteleev 和 Gleb Kalachev 也独立地造出了，用的是高维扩展图。<bookmark mark='d'/>Panteleev 和 Kalachev 的构造还给出了第一批好的量子 LDPC 码，回答了一个二十年的老问题。<bookmark mark='e'/>没有纠错，量子计算机根本无法工作，第53部分会讲到。<bookmark mark='f'/>而局部可测试码，正是第27部分的 PCP 定理的原料。

09802e796ca8.en: Six open problems. <bookmark mark='a'/> Whether any long binary codes beat the random ones of Gilbert and Varshamov. <bookmark mark='b'/> Where, between that bound and the linear-programming bound, the truth lies. <bookmark mark='c'/> Whether any explicit construction even matches random codes. <bookmark mark='d'/> How short a locally decodable code that reads three symbols can be. <bookmark mark='e'/> How close to capacity fast decoders can get at short lengths, which matter for control messages and the internet of things. <bookmark mark='f'/> And whether Reed-Muller codes reach capacity with an efficient decoder, not just in principle. <bookmark mark='g'/> This part's research problem takes a small, computable case of the fifth.
09802e796ca8.zh: 六个未解问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>是否有长的二元码能胜过 Gilbert 和 Varshamov 的随机码。<bookmark mark='b'/>在那个界和线性规划界之间，真相在哪里。<bookmark mark='c'/>是否有任何显式构造能哪怕追平随机码。<bookmark mark='d'/>只读三个符号的局部可解码码最短能有多短。<bookmark mark='e'/>快速解码器在短码长下能多接近容量，这对控制消息和物联网很重要。<bookmark mark='f'/>以及 Reed-Muller 码能否用高效的解码器达到容量，而不只是原则上可以。<bookmark mark='g'/>这一部分的研究题取第五个问题的一个小而可计算的情形。

73d6f751b24e.en: What we built in this part. The noisy channel and the repetition code. Hamming distance, and Hamming's code, whose syndrome names the bad bit. The bounds on how good any code can be, and the perfect Golay code, enumerated. The field of bytes, Reed-Solomon codes decoded by Berlekamp and Welch, and our own QR code, scratched three ways. CRCs from Part 5's shift registers. Shannon's theorem, watched in random codes. And the codes that reach his limit: Viterbi's trellis, an LDPC waterfall, and polarization.
73d6f751b24e.zh: 这一部分我们搭建了什么。有噪信道和重复码。汉明距离，以及伴随式能说出坏位的汉明码。任何码能好到什么程度的界，以及被逐一列举的完美 Golay 码。字节的域，用 Berlekamp 和 Welch 的方法解码的 Reed-Solomon 码，以及我们自己的二维码，被三种方式划伤。用第5部分的移位寄存器搭成的 CRC。在随机码上看到的 Shannon 定理。以及达到他的极限的那些码：Viterbi 的网格图、LDPC 的瀑布和极化。

f518d357d5e5.en: Where this comes back. Part 29 builds AES, whose S-box is inversion in the field of bytes. Part 30's secret sharing splits a key with exactly a Reed-Solomon code. Part 34 puts RAID and checksums into file systems, Part 36 puts a CRC on every Ethernet frame, and Part 45 computes how long erasure-coded cloud storage survives. And Part 53 needs codes to make quantum computers work at all.
f518d357d5e5.zh: 这些内容在哪里再次出现。第29部分搭建 AES，它的 S 盒就是字节域中的求逆。第30部分的秘密共享，用的正是一个 Reed-Solomon 码来拆分密钥。第34部分把 RAID 和校验和放进文件系统，第36部分给每个以太网帧加上 CRC，第45部分计算纠删编码的云存储能存活多久。而第53部分需要编码，量子计算机才能工作。

e9b547ee696a.en: In practice. Detect errors everywhere, with a CRC or checksum, and retry when it fails. Correct them where retrying is impossible or too slow: memory, deep space, broadcast. Prefer erasures: if you know what is missing, a code repairs twice as much. Choose replication when repairs must be fast, and erasure codes when storage costs dominate. And use a tested library: the arithmetic is easy to get subtly wrong, which is why we checked ours against zlib and a QR library.
e9b547ee696a.zh: 实践中。处处检测错误，用 CRC 或校验和，失败就重试。在重试不可能或太慢的地方纠正错误：内存、深空、广播。优先利用擦除：如果你知道缺了什么，码能修复两倍的量。修复必须快时选复制，存储成本为主时选纠删码。并且使用经过测试的库：这些运算很容易出微妙的错，这也是为什么我们拿自己的实现与 zlib 和一个二维码库对照。

401407b99d13.en: Six problems, with full solutions in the part's notes. Pause on any of them. The fifth is a build problem: a smaller QR code, made with this part's functions and read by your phone. The last, marked with a star, is a research problem: its answer is not known, and the notes say where to start.
401407b99d13.zh: 六道习题，完整解答在本部分的笔记里。可以在任何一题上暂停。第五题是动手题：用本部分的函数做一个更小的二维码，再用你的手机读出来。最后一题标了星号，是研究题：它的答案还不知道，笔记里写了从哪里入手。

5839fee4dda1.en: Next time: secrets. Codes in this part fought random noise. Part 29 faces an adversary. From frequency analysis and the Enigma to Shannon's perfect secrecy, and then AES, built from scratch on the same field of bytes, with the modes, hashes and message authentication codes that make it safe to use. Part 29, Secrets.
5839fee4dda1.zh: 下一次：秘密。这一部分的码对抗的是随机噪声。第29部分面对的是一个对手。从频率分析和恩尼格玛机，到 Shannon 的完美保密，再到从零搭建的 AES，建在同一个字节域上，配上让它能安全使用的工作模式、哈希和消息认证码。第29部分，秘密。

9bd24692775d.en: The books and papers this part follows are on screen and in the notes. Thank you for watching.
9bd24692775d.zh: 这一部分所依据的书籍和论文都在屏幕上和笔记里。感谢观看。
